name: Optimal AI (formerly Tara AI)
description: Optimal AI, formerly Tara AI, is an engineering-intelligence and agentic code-review platform for software teams. It connects repository and project data to review code, surface security and quality findings, explain delivery trends, measure cycle time and help teams improve engineering workflows.
agentUseSummary: Optimal AI publishes a local Optibot CLI and stdio MCP package for reviewing a developer's working tree, branch or diff file with a customer-owned API key. Relay cannot safely publish that raw local process from Railway because it requires repository filesystem authority, transmits source diffs and also exposes login and API-key administration; no supported bounded remote API contract is published for a typed cloud connector.

blocked.label: Connect Optimal AI
blocked.description: The published integration is a local CLI or stdio MCP process, not a bounded remote customer API that Railway can call safely.

blocked.label: Send code for review
blocked.description: Relay will not transmit repository changes, branches, patches or arbitrary diff files without an explicit supported data contract, source authority and redaction boundary.

blocked.label: Read a local workspace
blocked.description: Railway has no authority over a customer's developer working tree, Git branches or local patch files, and execution will not silently fall back to a device filesystem.

blocked.label: Manage Optibot credentials
blocked.description: The raw MCP package's login, logout, API-key creation, listing and deletion tools are administrative and unavailable to Relay agents.

blocked.label: Mount raw Optibot tools
blocked.description: Relay will not mount the provider's complete local MCP or CLI surface, execute model-selected commands or install an unreviewed latest npm package at runtime.

blocked.label: Automate private Optimal AI interfaces
blocked.description: Relay will not scrape the Optimal AI app, replay private traffic, reuse browser sessions or infer undocumented backend endpoints.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Optimal AI actions can be enabled until the provider supplies a bounded remote integration contract or Relay approves a version-pinned device-local source-host design with explicit repository and data-egress authority.

runtimeSupport.description: Optimal AI's local CLI/MCP requires developer-workspace filesystem access and includes credential administration; it cannot be mounted raw into OpenClaw or executed from Railway.
Optimal AI's local CLI/MCP requires developer-workspace filesystem access and includes credential administration; it cannot be mounted raw into Hermes or executed from Railway.

providerSetup.blocker: Optimal AI documents a customer-owned optk_ API key for its local Optibot CLI and stdio MCP package. That process reads local Git changes, branches and diff files, sends code to the provider review engine and also exposes authentication and API-key administration. The public docs do not provide a direct bounded HTTP API, request/response schema, source-host authorization model, redaction contract or version-pinned distributable lifecycle suitable for Relay's Railway runtime.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request an Optimal AI key and do not show Connect. In the separate provider-console acceptance task, ask Optimal AI for either a supported bounded remote review API contract or a formally supported version-pinned local source-host integration contract covering repository selection, explicit source authority, diff limits, redaction, data egress and retention, package integrity, review schemas, rate limits, audit, key rotation/revocation and removal of credential-administration tools; then re-run convergence.

evidence.supports: Optimal AI describes its current engineering-intelligence and Optibot code-review platform across repositories, security findings, delivery metrics and engineering workflows.

The official Optibot MCP documentation identifies a locally running stdio package, optk_ API-key authentication, local working-tree, branch and diff-file review tools, and login plus API-key administration tools.
Optimal AI documents a long-lived organization-bound API key and local CLI review/scan commands for agents and CI/CD, with the provider backend defaulting to agents.getoptimal.ai.

An official Optimal AI product article refers to the same engineering product as Tara AI and identifies its author as Optimal AI's CTO and co-founder, supporting the renamed-provider continuity decision.
The official tara.ai status domain now brands the service as Optimal AI and reports Optimal AI Insights, further supporting canonicalization under the current product identity.
Optimal AI says its services process source code, repository and project metadata, prompts, OAuth tokens and engineering metrics, confirming the sensitive data-egress and authority boundary.
